Hi Neha —

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for powering a mix of conversational support and multi-lingual summarization at DataLoop. Two quick asks up front:

1) Can you share the hosted API baseline rate card for text-gen and chat models, including how tokens are counted for billing?
2) We use SentencePiece tokenization for several of our pipelines. Does that change the way we should think about per-token billing vs BPE-based models (e.g., gpt-family or BPE variants)? Any typical conversion factors you recommend we use when estimating cost?

A bit of context: our pilot corpus is ~40M words (English + Spanish + Hindi), and our expected usage profile is bursty: 200–600 tps during business hours, ~10% of that overnight. Procurement timeline is tight — aiming to finalize vendor and MSA by the third week of March. We're also open to a committed spend discount but need to understand how to model costs when tokenization differs between models.

If it's easier, happy to hop on a 30-min call this week — otherwise a short write-up would be great.

Hi Claire —

Really appreciate the context. I put together a concise summary here and attached two artifacts: our public rate card (Redwood_Ratecard_v1.pdf) and a token sample we ran through our internal tokenizer so you can see token counts by model (tokenization-sample.csv). Quick highlights below — happy to drill in on any item.

How billing works (baseline)
- Hosted API billing = per input token + per output token (we bill both directions). Prices are model-dependent (we publish per-1k-token rates on the attached rate card).
- For multi-turn chat, we include the conversation history tokens in the usage calculation (standard industry approach).

Tokenization differences (high-level)
- Tokenization is model & tokenizer dependent. SentencePiece (subword) and BPE produce different token counts for the same text; differences vary by language and text morphology.
- Empirically we've seen ratios that range roughly from 0.85x to 1.25x when comparing SentencePiece vs our reference BPE tokenizers across varied corpora. Important caveat: the delta depends a lot on language and whitespace conventions (Indic languages and highly agglutinative text can skew the factor).

Practical guidance for cost modeling
- Run a representative sample through the tokenizer for each target model. The sample we attached shows per-model token counts side-by-side. Use those to compute effective $/k-token for your workload.
- If you expect to switch models in production (e.g., cheaper quantized variants vs higher-quality chat models), compute a weighted average tokenization factor by expected request mix.

Committed discounts & packaging (proposal)
- Baseline (no commit): see attached rate card.
- Committed monthly spend tiers (hosted API, applied at account level):
  * $50k/month commit → 10% discount on hosted API token rates
  * $150k/month commit → 15% discount
  * $300k/month commit → 22% discount + prioritized capacity during bursts
- Discounts apply to billed token usage for the specified account ID; overage beyond the commit is billed at the post-discount rate for that month up to the committed amount, then at the standard list rate for true overage (we can also structure yearly true-ups — see MAF draft attached).

Next steps I recommend
- If you can share ~10k–50k lines of a representative text sample (or allow us to tokenize one directly), we'll run the sample across candidate models and return a per-model token conversion table and expected monthly bill estimates for the mixes you suggested.
- If the procurement timeline is firm, we can draft a mutual action plan (I've attached a draft MAF) and a quote reflecting the discount tiers above.

Would you like us to proceed with tokenizing a sample? I can also schedule a 30-min call with our product/sales engineering folks.

Thanks,
Neha

Claire — quick note from the SE side: when we run your sample through our in-house tokenizers we measure both the tokenizer output and the effective billing tokens using the same truncation/rounding rules our billing engine applies. A couple of practical notes:
- We round tokenization counts the same way as billing (we apply per-request token rounding to the nearest integer and aggregate per-account for the billing window).
- For multi-byte/utf-8 inputs, the tokenizer choice can create sub-token fragmentation; we report the raw token count and the billed token count so you can see the delta.

Karthik — can you run the sample Claire shares (or the attached small CSV) and confirm the per-model ratio numbers in the CSV? I'll consolidate into a short cost-estimate table for Claire's team.

Thanks,
